lines.text: Maya’s agent just learned how to fix a flaky build. Sam’s agent, one desk over, is about to learn it all over again.
Multiply that by every teammate and every lesson. Hours go to rediscovering what somebody already knows.
Teams fixes that. You share workspaces with your teammates, and you choose how much of each one to share.
First, you see each other’s tasks live, so nobody asks what the other person is working on.
Next, memory. Agents can read the notes their teammates have saved, so a lesson only has to be learned once.
Skills can be shared as well, so the whole team edits one playbook, instead of everyone keeping a private copy.
And the Pano docs. Share a plan with the team on one board, one doc at a time.
Now Sam’s agent reads Maya’s memory, finds the fix, and skips the whole detour.
It clears the cache, the build goes green, and an afternoon of work becomes a minute.
Nothing is shared by default. Every switch is yours, and you can turn each one off again at any time.
What has one of your agents learned that the rest of your team still does not know? Tell us below, and try Teams at Agent R Q dot com.
